description:
Create a depth color-coded Z-projection of a confocal microscopy stack to visualize 3D structure.

Starting with the loaded 'FluorescentCells.tif' hyperstack (3 channels, 512x512, Z-stack):

1. Extract Channel 2 (Green/Cytoskeleton) from the hyperstack.
2. Pre-process the extracted stack:
   - Apply Background Subtraction (Rolling ball radius: 30 pixels)
   - Enhance Contrast (Saturated: 0.3%, Normalize)
3. Create a standard Maximum Intensity Projection (MIP) first and save it as '~/Fiji_Data/results/depth_projection/standard_mip.png'.
4. Apply Depth Color Coding to the stack:
   - Use Image > Hyperstacks > Temporal-Color Code
   - Select the 'Spectrum' LUT (or Fire/Ice)
   - This creates an RGB image where color represents Z-depth.
5. Add a calibration bar/legend to the result (Analyze > Tools > Calibration Bar) to map colors to depth.
6. Save the final color-coded projection as '~/Fiji_Data/results/depth_projection/depth_coded_projection.png'.
7. Save a text report to '~/Fiji_Data/results/depth_projection/stack_report.txt' listing: original number of channels, number of Z-slices, and the LUT name used.

Goal: Two images (grayscale MIP and RGB depth-coded) and one report file.
